info.title: Hypervalent Public API
info.summary: The token-authenticated content delivery and authoring API behind Hypervalent Studio.
info.description:
Every route lives under `/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{projectSlug}/…` — the project is a **required path segment**, never a query
parameter — except the two org-level discovery reads (`/token`, `/projects`). Authenticate with an organization API token
(`atk_…`) in `Authorization: Bearer` or `X-API-Key`. Bodies are JSON with camelCase keys. Read responses for organizations
without the `removeBranding` entitlement carry a `poweredBy` string.

This document is generated from the server's route table and token allow-list; the schemas are hand-authored beside
the shapers they describe. See https://docs.hypervalent.io/api/ for the guide.

post.description: Edit an atom in the working view (draft or published; trashed is a 404). Every key of `AtomWrite` is optional and an omitted key is left alone; the checks run against the atom as it will be, so a new `fieldType` re-checks the stored `fieldConfig` and `defaultValue` (resend them when they no longer fit; `defaultValue: null` clears it). While the atom is bound in a molecule, document type or taxonomy its `fieldType` and `multiple` cannot change, and `status: draft` is 409 `CANNOT_DRAFT_IN_USE`.

post.description: Edit up to 200 EXISTING tokens by slug in one transaction — tokens are never created or trashed through the API. `schemeValues` keys replace the stored ones and the rest are kept: a color role is keyed by scheme slug (hex values), a palette by tone, every other type by `default` — a CSS string, a typography composite (merged by property; `fontFamily` names a font-family set), or a component's `{ ref: '<group>.<token>' }` / `{ value }`. A color edit stamps `valueSource: manual` so regeneration keeps it; `valueSource: generated` hands the color back to the generator and regenerates. `status` moves a token between `draft` and `published` (publishing a component's tokens adds it to the export). Every problem is reported at once as 422 with `issues`; nothing is written until all pass.

401.description: `API_TOKEN_REQUIRED` — no credential; `INVALID_API_TOKEN` — revoked, expired, unknown, or another organization's token (nested `{ error }` envelope from the authenticator).

402.description: `BILLING_TERMINATED` — the organization's subscription was terminated for non-payment.

403.description: `TOKEN_ORG_MISMATCH` / `TOKEN_PROJECT_MISMATCH` — the credential does not cover the URL's org or project; `ACCOUNT_CLOSED`; `DELIVERY_BLOCKED` — content delivery for the organization is blocked by the platform ; `TOKEN_SCOPE_READ_ONLY` — a `read` token (carries `requiredPlan`); `FEATURE_DISABLED` — the plan has no API writes (carries `requiredPlan`)

404.description: `NOT_FOUND` — unknown org id, project slug, or resource. Never distinguishes "does not exist" from "not published".

409.description: `VERSION_LOCKED` — an editor holds the checkout (`holder.name`, `expiresAt`; nothing was written); `SLUG_CONFLICT` — the slug is taken. Also: CANNOT_DRAFT_IN_USE.

422.description: `VALIDATION_ERROR` — the payload was refused; `fields` names each problem. Nothing was written.

429.description: `RATE_LIMITED` — the per-credential limit was hit. `Retry-After` says how long to wait; draft-8 `RateLimit` headers name the policy.

500.description: `QUERY_FAILED` — the read or write could not complete. Never an empty 200.

503.description: `PLATFORM_READ_ONLY` / `PLATFORM_MAINTENANCE` — writes are paused platform-wide; `Retry-After` says how long.

get.description: The presented token's scope, project narrowing, expiry and the public feature trio. A project-narrowed token is a valid caller here (there is no path project to mismatch) and is confined instead.
